title: Windows key custody: Credential Manager KeyProvider, gated on its T26 run
description: Operator ruling 2026-09-28, relayed by opum-agent (OPAG-675) and binding once opum-doc records it: Windows is a committed platform. The spec never mentioned Windows. Key custody goes through Windows Credential Manager via a native API, never a command whose argv carries the key. Windows is not advertised until its own T26 qualification run passes. It needs a Windows packaged binary and a Windows runner or machine, and CI has neither today (CI is self-hosted Linux ARM64). Do not build this before WCLI-5 and WCLI-6.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Windows KeyProvider stores the vault key in Credential Manager, with the backend and its access semantics measured the way WCLI-5 measured the macOS Keychain
A locked or unavailable credential store fails closed within a bounded time and never waits on a hidden prompt
T26 on Windows: a real native key-provider integration run and a packaged-binary smoke test pass on Windows; mocked unit tests do not count
Windows is advertised as supported only after that T26 run, and the run is cited where it is advertised

implementationNotes: The platform ruling is recorded in opum-doc as ODOC-316 (docs/adr/wards-committed-platform-target-macos-linux-and-windows.md, opum-doc main 900319d), and this repository's docs/adr/0004-committed-platform-target.md states it (WCLI-23).

WCLI-20 review, 2026-09-28: same setup-lock fallback race as WCLI-21's note — the non-darwin O_EXCL pid fallback must be replaced with kernel-arbitrated or identity-checked locking before Windows is qualified.
Grooming 2026-10-28 (opum-doc approved via team-lead): re-ranked to the bottom (priority low, ordinal 9999 after every other task), kept.

From the opus APPROVE at 9ee8b83 of ward-cli#254 (WCLI-125), unverified item, recorded 2026-11-03: fs.constants.O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW are undefined on Windows in Node (Bun unknown), so bindCheckoutIdentity's open of the ward directory (src/adapters/checkout.ts, the O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW open before the nonce file is created) degrades there to a plain O_RDONLY directory open. That either refuses every registration (if opening a directory fails) or silently drops the link check the earlier lstat gave. No Windows CI shows which. The Windows port must handle it, for example by falling back to the lstat check when the flags are absent. Nothing ships on Windows today, so this is not a blocker now.
